key_idea: The volume of a prism under a triangle is area*(h0+h1+h2)/3, so the total is linear in the heights: each outer hole has weight (sum of its two adjacent triangle areas)/3 and the centre has weight (total area)/3; by the rearrangement inequality pair sorted heights with sorted weights.
sketch: Sort the n-1 holes by angle, compute the area of each triangle (origin, hole i, hole i+1) by the cross product, accumulate the area into both endpoints' weights and into the centre's weight. Sort the n weights and the n heights and sum the products, divide by 3. O(n log n). Pitfalls: recognizing that no search is needed despite n<=30 suggesting it; the centre pole is not automatically the tallest (an outer hole may have a larger weight only if its two triangles exceed half the area, which cannot happen, but sorting handles it anyway); print with enough decimals.
